Zambia · Contact

Talk to us about your wayleave, right of way or licence area in Zambia

Tell us about the line, route, reserve or licence area and what the record is for. We reply by email with the questions we need answered, and then with a written proposal covering the scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

About you
About the route or site

What do you need?

Location or province, the buffer distances to check, and any date the record must reflect.

Your request reaches us through FormSubmit, a form-delivery service. Read the privacy notice.

What happens next

  1. We reply by email to confirm what we need from you.
  2. A short scoping call about the route or site, the distances that matter and the imagery.
  3. A written proposal: scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

What to send

The route or boundary file (KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage), the country and province, the distances to check, the date the record must reflect, the deliverables you need and your deadline. No file yet? Describe the location and we can draw the route with you.

Procurement teams

Send your supplier or prequalification forms, or the tender documents, with your request. The proposal states which registrations are in place for your contract and which are being arranged.

For a line, route or site in Zambia

  • The province and district, so we can check the imagery that exists for the area.
  • The asset: a power line and its voltage, a petroleum pipeline, a railway or road, or a mining licence area, and the file you have for it.
  • The widths to report: the SI 2 of 2026 wayleave for the voltage, the forestry width where a line crosses a recognised forestry area, your easement or reserve widths, or the consent distances around planned mine workings. Up to six widths in one survey.
  • The date the record must reflect, such as a cut-off date, the date a wayleave was acquired or the start of rehabilitation.
  • Your own imagery: whether your teams already fly drones, and the dates of the latest orthophotos.
  • Satellite only, or drone detail too. Drone work needs a Zambian operator with an ROC and an Air Services Permit, a special authorisation and Air Force clearance for each operation, so the proposal shows the lead time. See drone law in Zambia.
  • Protected status: whether the corridor or site is a declared protected area or place, and who authorises work on it.
  • Who should receive the results, so they go only to the contacts you name.

Frequently asked questions

Do you need a site visit or a drone flight to start?

No. A survey in Zambia starts from your route or boundary file and dated satellite imagery, open building datasets or the orthophotos you already hold, so nobody travels and no aircraft flies. Drone detail is added only where a stretch needs it, subject to the ZCAA approvals and Zambia Air Force clearance each operation requires, which the proposal shows in the timeline.

Our corridor or site is a declared protected area or place. Can we still ask?

Yes. Tell us in your request, and who in your organisation authorises work on it. We work on protected corridors and sites only for, or with the written authority of, the operator or licence holder, results go only to the contacts you name, and security sites are masked in every deliverable.

Can we send our own drone orthophotos?

Yes. Tell us roughly how many kilometres or hectares they cover, the capture dates and the format, and we check a sample before we commit. Large files are transferred by a link you choose or one we send; the form is for your request, not for imagery.

We have no route file yet. Can we still ask?

Yes. Describe the line, pipeline or road, the province and district it crosses, or send tower, valve or kilometre-post coordinates, and we draw the route with you and send it back for your confirmation before any survey runs.

Our procurement runs through ZPPA e-GP or our own supplier portal. Can you respond there?

Name the portal and the tender or reference number in your request, and send any supplier-registration, local-content or data-protection forms your organisation uses. Our notes for procurement teams set out what applies to this kind of service in Zambia.
